tasks.title: telemetry: record shape, identity, JSONL sink

details.goal: The three decisions a telemetry record needs before any buffer exists: what fields it carries, which install it belongs to, and which file it lands in.
details.contract:
Port src/shared/telemetry/{record,identity,sink}.ts (359 + 234 + 50 lines).
record.rs: RECORD_VERSION = 1; three kinds call, index_run, session; whitelist copies only, every field always present, in declaration order.
CallRecord fields in order: ts, v, kind, install_id, session_id, seq, tool, status, error_code, duration_ms, arg_names_set[], budget_tokens, payload_tokens, budget_used_ratio, truncated, truncation_reason, total_relation, coverage_complete, coverage_indexed, coverage_skipped, coverage_failed, unresolved_edges, stale, stale_reason, generation_age_ms, result_counts{}, server_version, bun_version, os, arch, graph_schema_version.
IndexRunRecord: ts, v, kind, install_id, session_id, mode, exit_code, duration_ms, was_forced, generation_advanced, files_seen, files_indexed, files_skipped, files_failed, nodes_by_kind{}, edges_by_kind_tier{}, unresolved_count, unresolved_ratio, languages{}, db_size_bytes, files_changed_in_run.
SessionRecord: ts, v, kind, install_id, session_id, session_mode, server_version, bun_version, os, arch, is_first_run, repo_size_bucket, languages[], root_kind.
THE FIELD NAME STAYS bun_version. It carries sangkar_core::runtime::runtime_version(). The report never reads it (src/shared/telemetry/report.ts:277-311), so a rename would buy nothing and would change a v1 record shape that the parity bar forbids changing; put that reasoning in a comment above the field.
Derivations copied verbatim: payload_tokens = ceil(bytes of compact JSON / 4); budget_used_ratio rounded to 4 decimals; an unknown stale_reason becomes other; result_counts maps each array-valued payload key to its length; generation_advanced = exit_code == 0; unresolved_ratio = unresolved / (unresolved + sum(edges_by_kind_tier)); repo_size_bucket and root_kind use the written thresholds.
identity.rs: <dir>/install_id.json = an object with install_id (32 hex) and date (YYYY-MM-DD), created with create_new (EEXIST means another process won the race, which is fine), a stale file removed first, new_session_id() 32 hex, utc_date_of from the record's own timestamp.
sink.rs: <dir>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl, one append of the joined lines plus a trailing newline, zero lines writes nothing.
Tests: the exact JSON of one record of each kind with key order asserted, the runtime field present under its original name, the ratio and rounding cases, the identity race, and an append that never rewrites an existing file.
steps: Port record.rs with one struct per kind and the two builders.
Fill bun_version from runtime_version() and add the comment explaining why the name stays.
Port identity.rs with create_new and the stale-file removal.
Port sink.rs and the date split.
Write the tests asserting the exact serialized bytes of three records.
details.verify:
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-telemetry --test record_sink exits 0.
Done when: the serialized call record's key order equals the TypeScript one exactly, the field is still named bun_version, and docs/my-product/TELEMETRY.md is untouched.

tasks.title: telemetry: the loopback report server and the `telemetry` verb

details.goal: Serve the report on loopback and write it to a file, with the flags, the refusal and the two stdout lines the CLI answers today.
details.contract:
Port `src/shared/telemetry/{serve,cli}.ts` (205 + 222 lines).
`serve.rs`: `DEFAULT_REPORT_PORT = 7317`; hosts limited to `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost` (any other host is a usage refusal, not a bind attempt); one HTTP listener answering `GET /` with `text/html`, re-rendering `render_multi_report` per request from `<home>`'s registry roots; `{"url", "port", "host", "repositories"}` returned on start; `stop()` releases the port.
`telemetry_cmd.rs`: flags `--out` (default `<dataDir>/telemetry/report.html`), `--serve`, `--port`, `--host`, `--since`, plus the inert globals; `--serve` and `--out` are mutually exclusive (usage refusal); stdout is exactly `wrote <path> (<n> records, <m> unparsed lines)` or `serving <url> (<n> repositories)`; exit `0` success, `2` usage, `1` write failure.
Tests: a bind on port 0 then a `GET /` returning 200 with `text/html` and a body containing a panel id; a bound non-loopback host refused with exit 2; the mutual-exclusion refusal; and the `wrote …` line for a temp directory with two records and one malformed line.
steps: Port the listener with the one route and the loopback allow-list.
Port the per-request re-render from the registry.
Port the verb's flag parsing, the mutual exclusion and the two stdout lines.
Write the tests, closing the server at the end of each.
details.verify:
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-telemetry --test serve exits 0 and leaves no listening socket behind.
Done when: sangkar telemetry --serve --port 0 prints a serving line whose URL answers 200 with text/html, and the body contains the eight panel markers tools, truncation, relations, coverage, argument-names, trend, index-runs and sessions (assert the marker names, not a line count).

tasks.title: daemon: status types and the single-daemon lifecycle

details.goal: One daemon at a time, on a pid lock, with start/stop/status that behave the way the TypeScript CLI already does — the piece that must never run twice after cutover.
details.contract:
Port `src/daemon/{types,lifecycle}.ts` (355 lines).
```rust
pub struct DaemonStatus { pub pid: Option<u32>, pub started_at: Option<String>, pub uptime_ms: Option<u64>,
  pub repositories: Vec<RepoRuntime>, pub report: Option<ReportAddress> }
pub struct RepoRuntime { pub root: String, pub watch: bool, pub last_run: Option<String>,
  pub last_exit: Option<i32>, pub generation: Option<String> }
pub fn run_daemon(opts: &DaemonOptions) -> i32;      // owns the pid lock until a signal
pub fn start(opts: &DaemonOptions) -> StartOutcome;  // spawns detached, waits for the lock to appear
pub fn stop(home: &Path) -> StopOutcome;             // SIGTERM, wait, then report
pub fn status(home: &Path) -> DaemonStatus;
```
Rules: the lock file is `<home>/daemon.pid` with `{"pid","startedAt"}` (same shape as phase 0 — the TypeScript daemon must be able to reclaim it); the daemon writes `<home>/daemon.log`; the loop ticks at `watch_interval` and heartbeats the pid lock; SIGINT/SIGTERM shut down cleanly (stop all watchers, close the report server, release the lock, exit 0); `start` refuses when a live lock exists and reports the holder's pid; `stop` refuses nothing but reports a stale pid honestly; the detached child must not inherit stdout (protocol discipline applies to the daemon too).
Tests: run/stop via a child process, `status` before and after, a second `start` refusal, a stale lock reclaim (dead pid), and a signal shutdown leaving no lock file.
steps: Port types.rs and the pid-lock wiring through `sangkar_core::pidlock`.
Port `run_daemon`'s loop, tick and signal handling.
Port `start` (detached spawn + wait for the lock) and `stop`.
Port `status` including the stale case.
Write the tests using a child process and temp home.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-daemon --test lifecycle` exits 0.
Done when: a second `start` while the first is alive reports the holder's pid and exit 1, and a stop leaves `<home>/daemon.pid` absent.

tasks.title: daemon: the reconciler, the composition order, the `daemon` verb

details.goal: Make the live watchers match `<home>/sangkar.json` on every pass, compose the daemon in the documented order, and answer the four subcommands with the same lines and exit codes.
details.contract:
Port `src/daemon/{reconcile,main,cli}.ts` (294 + 114 + 236 lines).
`reconcile`: one pass over the registry — start a watcher for a newly registered root, stop and forget one that was removed or whose watch flag turned off, keep an unchanged one untouched (no restart), and refresh the repo's config on a change. A failing startup for one root is logged and does not abort the pass. Watch interval per root comes from that repo's own config, clamped 1000..=300000.
`main`: composition order is lock -> reconciler -> report server -> loop; on shutdown the reverse order. The report server starts only when the machine config enables it and `--port`/`--host` are for `run` only.
`cli`: `daemon run|start|stop|status`; `run` blocks and logs to stderr (and `<home>/daemon.log`); `status --json` prints the `DaemonStatus` object; the plain forms print the same human lines as today. Exit `1` when `start` finds a live daemon, `2` for a bad subcommand or a flag given to the wrong subcommand.
Tests: a temp home with two registered repositories — a run indexes both, removing one from the registry stops exactly that watcher, adding one starts one, a repo whose watch flag is off never spawns, and `status --json` reports both roots.
steps: Port reconcile.rs with the three-case diff and the per-root interval.
Port main.rs's composition and shutdown order.
Port cli.rs with the four subcommands and the flag scoping.
Write the integration test using a temp home, two tiny fixtures and a fake worker command.
details.verify:
`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p sangkar-daemon --test integration` exits 0.
Done when: the test observes two watcher starts, one stop after the registry edit, and `status --json` carrying both roots with their last exit codes.

tasks.title: Phase 4 close: daemon and report behave as the TypeScript suite describes

details.goal: Prove the daemon owns exactly one pid lock, spawns one watcher per registered repository, and that the report renders the same numbers from the same records.
details.contract: Read-only except `rust/Cargo.lock`. Never leave a daemon or a listening socket behind: kill what you start, and check `<home>/daemon.pid` is absent at the end.
steps: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`.
Start the Rust daemon on a temp home with two registered fixtures, confirm two watchers and at least one index run, then `status --json`, then `stop`.
Generate a report from a telemetry directory containing both a legacy `bun_version` record and a new `runtime_version` record; confirm both are counted.
Run `~/.bun/bin/bun test` and diff against the TASK-015 baseline.
Report: watchers started, runs observed, records read, and any divergence from the TypeScript behaviour.
details.verify:
All gates exit 0; the daemon leaves no pid file; the report counts both record generations.
Done when: the report states the exact path of the pid file it checked, the number of runs observed, and `pgrep -f 'sangkar daemon'` returns nothing.
